narrative: This collection agency calls me 4 to 5 times a day, sometimes before 8am, about a payday loan debt. I have asked them multiple times to only contact me by mail and they keep calling anyway. It's gotten to the point where I'm afraid to answer my phone.
extracted_allegations: Collection agency calls 4 to 5 times a day | Calls sometimes occur before 8am | Calls concern a payday loan debt | Customer asked multiple times to be contacted only by mail and the agency continues to call | Customer is afraid to answer their phone
policy_cited: 08 General Dispute Handling Process (standard process, outcome classified as partially confirmed)
draft_text:
Thank you for telling us about the repeated phone calls from the collection agency on your payday loan debt. We understand how stressful it is to be afraid to pick up your own phone, and we looked carefully at what you described.

Here is what we found on each point:

1. Calls 4 to 5 times a day: Our call records confirm this. They show 4 calls on March 30, 2026 and 5 calls on March 31, 2026. A further call was answered on April 1, 2026 at 12:05.

2. Calls before 8am: Our records confirm this too. Calls were placed at 7:41am on March 30 and 7:55am on March 31.

3. The debt the calls are about: Our records show your payday loan account in collection, and a collection notice was mailed to you on March 2, 2026.

4. Your requests to be contacted by mail only: We could not confirm this. We found no record of a mail-only request in our account notes or history. A request made directly to the collection agency might not appear in our records. We also have no record of what was said on the April 1 call.

5. Your fear of answering the phone: We have noted what you shared about how these calls are affecting you.

Because we could not find a record of your mail-only request, we cannot confirm a mail-only contact preference on our side at this time. No other remedy has been approved on this complaint.

To help us look into this further, please reply to this message with when and how you asked to be contacted by mail only (for example, by phone or in writing), and who you spoke with if you remember. Copies of any letters or notes you kept would also help. You are welcome to send us anything further at any time, and we will review it.

narrative: My installment loan payment was due on the 14th and I paid it on the 13th through the mobile app. I still got charged a $35 late fee. I have a screenshot of the app showing the payment confirmation dated the 13th.
extracted_allegations: Charged a $35 late fee despite paying on the 13th, before the 14th due date
policy_cited: 06 Fee Waiver and Goodwill Credit Authority, $0–$50 tier (fee confirmed charged in error: payment received before due date but late fee still assessed)
draft_text:
You contacted us about a $35 late fee on your account, saying you paid on the 13th, a day before your payment was due on the 14th.

We reviewed your account records. They show your payment of $118.75 was received through the mobile app on April 13, 2026, one day before the April 14 due date. The payment was recorded on our ledger on April 15, and the $35 late fee was applied that same day. That recording delay appears to be why the fee was applied. Our records confirm the fee was applied in error.

We are waiving the $35 late fee. This falls within the amount our complaints analysts can approve, so no further sign-off is needed. Our own records show when your payment was received, so you don't need to send your app screenshot.

You don't need to do anything else. If you have anything further you'd like us to look at, you can send it at any time and we will review it. Please include your case reference number in any follow-up.

narrative: My account is showing as 60 days past due on my credit report, but I have never missed a payment on this account. My bank statements show every payment was made on time for the past 18 months.
extracted_allegations: Account is showing as 60 days past due on credit report | Customer states they have never missed a payment on this account
policy_cited: 04 Credit Reporting Disputes (FCRA): investigation timeline (30/45 days), what an agent may say, and remedy authority (no correction initiated because internal records support the reported status). Also Policy 10 (Prohibited Language) and Policy 11 (Response Tone and Format).
draft_text:
You contacted us because your account is showing as 60 days past due on your credit report, and you believe every payment has been made on time. Seeing a delinquency you don't expect on your credit report is worrying, so we reviewed your payment history in detail.

On the reported delinquency: our records show that the scheduled $140.00 installments due March 18, 2026 and April 18, 2026 were not received. On April 20, 2026, the account was reported as 60 days past due, which matches those two missed installments.

On your statement that you have never missed a payment: the records we reviewed, which run from January 18, 2026 to June 18, 2026, do not support this for March and April. On May 18, 2026 we received a $280.00 payment covering two installments, and the June 18, 2026 installment arrived on time. Your account now shows as current.

Because our records match what was reported, we have not made a correction to your account. We were not able to confirm from our records whether the credit bureau has updated its display since your May payment.

If your bank statements show payments on or around March 18 or April 18, 2026 that we haven't matched, please reply to this message with copies. We will review anything you send, and you are welcome to send further information at any time.

Disputes like this are investigated within 30 days. That can extend to 45 days if you give us additional information during that period. We control the information we report, but we can't control or give a date for when a credit bureau updates what it shows.

If you are not satisfied with the outcome, you can ask for a statement of your dispute to be added to your credit file. You are also free to contact any other organization about this, including a regulator.

Overdraft: We can't confirm this part from our records. No overdraft fee or related charge appears on your account with us, and we can't see activity on your bank account. Any overdraft would have been assessed by your bank, so your bank statement is the document that would show it.
